children: chairman Alex Reilley said Germany could become as large an opportunity as the UK for the hospitality group,

reported. The firm will open its first site in Essen this October and believes it could eventually roll out hundreds of venues across the country if the concept proves successful. Reilley, a vocal advocate for stronger high streets, said Germany's urban centres offer a more supportive environment than the UK, where he previously quit a government taskforce in protest at tax policy.
Alex Gerko paid himself a record £895m in 2025 after his trading firm

delivered £1.7bn in profits, The Telegraph reported. The remaining £833m was shared among 23 staff, averaging more than £36m each. XTX's revenue jumped 44% to £3.9bn amid volatile markets, lifting Gerko's pay by 31% year‑on‑year. HMRC collected £331.4m in tax from him last year, making him the UK's second‑largest taxpayer, according to
. Gerko has previously criticised the tax authority for "gloating" over high UK tax levels.
More than one in ten delivery riders stopped during a police immigration crackdown were found to be working illegally,
revealed. Officers checked around 1,482 couriers last summer, arresting at least 151 for working without authorisation, with 17 subsequently deported. Delivery apps such as
face tougher penalties from 1 October, when fines of £60,000 per illegal worker will be introduced under new legislation.

France risks edging towards a debt downgrade as government spending continues to outpace economic performance, according to

. Fitch reaffirmed the country's A+ rating but warned deficit projections had worsened due to weaker growth, rising interest costs and additional defence spending. The agency said political fragmentation ahead of the 2027 election remained a key constraint on fiscal progress. France lost its double‑A rating in 2025, though the euro's reserve‑currency status continues to provide a buffer by ensuring strong investor demand.
